item.title: New China-DPRK border bridge over Yalu River opens to traffic
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
An opening ceremony is held for a new bridge across the Yalu River, the border river of China and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on Oct. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Yulong) SHENYANG, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge officially opened to traffic on Thursday, with both sides jointly holding an opening ceremony on this cross-border artery. The cable-stayed bridge over the Yalu River serves as a cross-border transport link between the city of Dandong in northeast China's Liaoning Province and the city of Sinuiju in North Pyongan Province in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK). The double-pylon and double-cable-plane bridge features a 28.5-meter-wide deck designed with four lanes for two-way traffic, while its water navigation clearance is designed for vessels of up to the 3,000-tonne class. The new bridge will further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, and the new bridge is an important facility for connectivity between the two countries, Mao noted at a regular press briefing. Dandong boasts China's largest border trade port with the DPRK. Before the new road bridge, the Yalu River Bridge, also known as the China-DPRK Friendship Bridge, served as a combined road-rail bridge. The old one, however, could only accommodate trucks weighing no more than 20 tonnes for one-way road traffic. China and the DPRK in 2010 agreed to build a new road bridge downstream from the old one. ■ An opening ceremony is held for a new bridge across the Yalu River, the border river of China and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on Oct. 15, 2026. item.title: Across China: When yak milk meets coffee on China's Tibetan plateau
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
CHENGDU, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Gonbu never developed a taste for coffee, and that remains true to this day. But that hasn't stopped the 30-year-old Tibetan from opening a restaurant that serves coffee with a local twist: yak milk, highland barley and butter. Growing up on the grasslands of southwest China's Sichuan Province, Gonbu spent his childhood days riding horses and herding yaks. He had never even heard of coffee. Today, he is bringing the flavors of his childhood to visitors in the ancient town of Songpan, hoping to ignite interest in the nomadic culture behind them. Gonbu runs a Tibetan restaurant in the town, which has a history spanning over 1,000 years. Located in Songpan County, where the average elevation exceeds 3,000 meters, the town was once a trading hub between southwestern and northwestern China. There, traders exchanged horses, medicinal herbs, and animal hides for tea and grain. Born in Caoyuan Village in Songpan's Maoergai Township, he later studied Tibetan-Chinese translation at Northwest Minzu University in Lanzhou, where he tried coffee for the first time. He was drawn to the atmosphere of coffee shops -- "somewhere you can read a book or just sit for a while," as he put it. He found similar places in other cities and wondered why the grasslands couldn't have one, too. In 2019, Gonbu returned to Maoergai and opened a small reading lounge serving coffee. "Young people on the grasslands also need somewhere to relax and learn about the outside world," he said. Over the next five years, he traveled to learn coffee-making and Tibetan cooking while studying how restaurants operated in cities. He kept thinking about Songpan's ancient town. The county is a gateway to the UNESCO World Heritage sites of Jiuzhai Valley and Huanglong, and the town now has more than 10 businesses established by returning college graduates. In late 2024, Gonbu opened the restaurant, hoping to offer visitors a fresh perspective on Tibetan cuisine and nomadic life. Inside, sheepskins are draped over the chairs, and ingredients are sourced from the plateau whenever possible. Traditional Tibetan dishes share the menu with coffee made from barley, yak milk, butter and yak yogurt. By day, customers eat, drink coffee and read. In the evening, traditional ethnic music alternates with modern folk songs. Gonbu wants the restaurant to offer more than just food and entertainment. He teaches his staff to make coffee and has filled the restaurant with books. Of his 18 employees, 12 come from Maoergai. Their average age is just 22 to 23. One is 18-year-old Tsering Drolkar. Had she not come to the ancient town, she said, she would probably be herding yaks at home. Collecting medicinal herbs can sometimes bring in good money. "I just want to go out and see more of the world," she said. Since arriving, she has learned to make coffee, played the guitar for the first time and encountered unfamiliar foods. At 11, she traveled beyond the grasslands for the first time, visiting her father's hometown of Mianyang in Sichuan. Before the trip, she had heard stories of watermelons, bananas and other fruits rarely seen back home. Today, leaving the remote highlands is easier. Nine decades ago, crossing them was a struggle for survival. In 1935, the Communist Party of China-led Red Army entered northwest Sichuan during the Long March, a roughly 12,500-kilometer military odyssey from 1934 to 1936. The soldiers crossed the marshy grasslands of what are now Songpan, Hongyuan, Ruoergai and surrounding areas. In his book "The Long March: The Untold Story," American journalist and author Harrison Salisbury described the area as "untouched for 3,000 years." With its swamps, extreme cold and low oxygen levels, the treacherous terrain claimed the lives of many soldiers. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the Long March's victory. Gonbu's grandparents lived through that era and passed down stories of the Red Army. "With transportation being so convenient today, it's really hard to imagine what they went through back then," he said. On Aug. 30, 2024, a new section of the Sichuan-Qinghai railway opened, bringing bullet train services to Songpan. From Huanglong-Jiuzhai station, a short drive from the ancient town, the fastest trains reach Chengdu in about one hour and 40 minutes. Near the station stands a memorial park commemorating the Long March. A statue depicts a Red Army soldier raising a rifle and flowers. Nearby, modern trains speed past. The grasslands are now drawing more visitors. Songpan County received 10.64 million tourist visits in 2025, up 15.53 percent year on year, with total tourism spending reaching 31.81 billion yuan (about 4.73 billion U.S. dollars). Visitors now come for more than scenery. They ride horses, hike, watch the stars or stop for coffee in the ancient town. The shift toward experiencing local life reflects the growing popularity of immersive tourism in China. The outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), released in March, calls for closer integration of culture and tourism and a wider range of high-quality tourism offerings. For Gonbu, a cup of yak milk coffee is only a starting point. If customers wonder where the milk comes from, he hopes to take them to Maoergai to see the yaks, pastures and people who produce it. He plans to build a ranch there with a reading lounge, bringing together food, tourism and herding life. "Tradition and modernity, the countryside and the city -- they can all come together in a place like this," he said. ■

item.title: China willing to promote trade in dual-use items with EU: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- China is ready to work with the European Union (EU) to continue to leverage the role of the export control dialogue mechanism and promote the development of bilateral trade in dual-use items, a spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday. Ministry spokesperson He Yadong made the remarks at a regular press conference in response to a media question about rare earth export licensing to the EU. China is willing to continue to provide facilitation for the approval of rare earth export licenses to the EU, and hopes the EU will offer facilitation for the reciprocal resolution of key licensing cases concerning China in the dual-use field, He said. ■

item.title: China's Zhuque-2E rocket launches 10 satellites into space
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
A Zhuque-2E Y4 carrier rocket carrying 10 satellites blasts off from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China, Oct. 14, 2026. China successfully launched a Zhuque-2E Y4 carrier rocket from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China on Wednesday. The rocket lifted off at 7:40 p.m. (Beijing Time) and deployed 10 satellites into their preset orbits. The flight test mission was declared a complete success. (Photo by Wang Jiangbo/Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China successfully launched a Zhuque-2E Y4 carrier rocket from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China on Wednesday. The rocket lifted off at 7:40 p.m. (Beijing Time) and deployed 10 satellites into their preset orbits. The flight test mission was declared a complete success. Eight satellites of the 02 group of a "star compute" plan, developed by Adaspace Technology Co., Ltd. (ADAspace) and designed to operate in dawn-dusk orbits, were included in the launch. According to ADAspace, a commercial aerospace enterprise, these satellites carry high-performance computing payloads, high-speed inter-satellite and satellite-to-ground laser communication payloads, low-light cameras and other equipment. They will conduct in-orbit verification of key technologies, such as liquid-cooled fluid loops at the 10,000-watt level, ultra-large deployable radiative cooling wings, full-domain laser communication networks and in-orbit training of foundation models. ADAspace said it intends to carry out in-orbit tests of the 02 group satellites, advance technological iteration, and promote the space computing technology innovation and industry innovation. The "star compute" plan is an ambitious project by the company to build AI space infrastructure composed of 2,800 computing satellites. The first group of satellites for the plan was successfully launched in May 2025. The third group is scheduled for orbital deployment in 2026. ■ A Zhuque-2E Y4 carrier rocket carrying 10 satellites blasts off from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China, Oct. 14, 2026. item.title: China's foreign trade maintains sound momentum as new drivers power exports
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade maintained sound momentum in the first three quarters of 2026, with both exports and imports growing rapidly and the overall growth rate reaching its highest level for the same period in five years, official data showed Wednesday. The country's total imports and exports rose 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan (about 5.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-September period, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). Growth accelerated through the year, with the expansion rate rising from 15.3 percent in the first quarter to 18.3 percent in the second quarter and 22.3 percent in the third quarter. Foreign trade growth in the first three quarters was the fastest for the same period in the past five years, with both quarterly and monthly growth rates generally accelerating, said Wang Jun, GAC's deputy head. "Latest international data show that such a growth rate ranks among the top among major economies, and China remains the world's largest trader of goods," the official told a press conference on Wednesday. Wang said the performance could be summed up in four words: "fast, new, quality and open." Describing the "new," he noted that trade in industrial robots, electronic components, computer parts and electrical equipment exceeded 10 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, up 58.9 percent and driving overall import and export growth by 11.3 percentage points. Exports increased 16.4 percent year on year to 23.2 trillion yuan, while imports expanded by 22.3 percent to 16.74 trillion yuan, GAC data showed. In September alone, China's total imports and exports reached 5.16 trillion yuan, up 27.5 percent from a year earlier and crossing the 5-trillion-yuan mark for the first time. This figure also marked the sixth consecutive month of double-digit monthly growth. Exports rose 29.6 percent year on year to 3.03 trillion yuan, while imports grew 24.6 percent to 2.13 trillion yuan for the month. Exports continued to shift toward smarter and greener products. Integrated circuit exports surged 99.1 percent year on year in the first three quarters, while exports of electric vehicles, lithium batteries, and wind power generating sets and their parts rose 72.3 percent, 36.4 percent and 22.4 percent, respectively. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year. After completing simulated spray-painting tests on vehicle bodies, a batch of its spraying robots will be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. "We provide well-known automakers like Maserati and Volkswagen with integrated robotics solutions for smart production, covering painting, welding, precision assembly and the handling of materials," said You Wei, EFORT's chairman and CEO, adding that EFORT's overseas robot business has grown at a compound annual growth rate of nearly 100 percent over the past three years. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the trade expansion. Their total imports and exports rose 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period, with intermediate goods trade up 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan and high-tech product exports up 42.1 percent. Wang said more foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains. "The global AI investment boom has kept overseas demand firm, and rising prices will continue to drive rapid growth in chip exports, which is currently the main driver of China's export expansion," said Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Golden Credit Rating. He added that China's manufacturing upgrading has continued to boost exports of new energy vehicles and high-tech products. The country's trade with more than 180 countries and regions expanded during the first three quarters. Trade with free trade partners reached 19.55 trillion yuan, up 30 percent and contributing over 70 percent of the total trade increment. Meanwhile, trade with other APEC economies rose 23.9 percent to 24.07 trillion yuan. Trade with ASEAN grew 22.7 percent to 6.84 trillion yuan, that with the European Union rose 8.4 percent to 4.78 trillion yuan, and trade with the United States increased 4.1 percent to 3.18 trillion yuan. Exports continued to shift toward new and higher-quality growth drivers. The equipment manufacturing sector contributed nearly 90 percent of the export increment, while intermediate goods accounted for more than half of total exports, underpinning global industrial and supply chains, according to the GAC. ■
